facts.text: Surveyor 3 was deployed at Ocean of Storms during Apollo 12 in 1967.

NASA's unmanned probe that soft-landed on 20 April 1967, two and a half years before Apollo 12. Conrad and Bean walked to it, inspected it, and cut off its TV camera to bring back to Earth. The rest of Surveyor 3 is still here.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
After 31 months on the Moon, its retrieved camera and soil scoop showed the effects of micrometeorite bombardment and solar radiation on hardware, providing data for long-duration spacecraft design.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Ocean of Storms.

The retrieved TV camera is on display at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum; analysis of bacteria reportedly found inside it sparked decades of scientific debate about contamination protocols.
